institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go on exchange to a university with an academic level that ensured my learning during the exchange. I also wished to experience and learn the French culture and language as well as get to know the famous city of Paris.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have enjoyed my stay, but I am dissatisfied with the circumstances that made it difficult to be able to study the language while being in Paris. Firstly, it is not possible to include language courses as a part of the programme by UoC-rules, secondly the work load of Sciences Po made it difficult to put much effort into self-studying language outside the 30-ECTS worth of courses.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, great communication through the Sciences Po email system

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mostly assistance by email. I was informed of where to go and ask if I needed further information or assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: In my case, it turned out to be very difficult. I started with a 1-month rental and the during the semester had to find a new place. Searching through different online housing pages and Facebook groups, I was in contact with about 120 different people in my hunt for housing. It also happened 5-6 times that I ended up in contact with scammers whose attempts were not easy to 'see through'. Eventually and at the very last minute, I luckily found a room with two other students close to the Eiffel tower, but also very costly - 1000€ a month.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: To some extent it is a game of luck. Don't be too picky as it may stop you from taking some opportunities that you would happily have accepted two weeks later. I at least had to lower my expectations during the process and also realise that I would have to pay 1000€ a month, even though that was much more than I had hoped.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The course registration was arbitrary and chaotic

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: For the course registration, you were told to be ready at an exact time (something like 10:21 a.m.). You had to be quick to get the courses you needed/wanted. It was important to be strategic and very well prepared, having already considered 2-3 alternatives for each of the courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: An overview of courses, their information (about teacher, course description, examination, etc.), and time of classes.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed to get most of the courses I wanted. One was quickly full and so I had to choose alternatives. Two weeks before the beginning of the semester, I received the message than one of my courses had been cancelled, and therefore I had to choose another course between the ones that still had extra spaces.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be very well prepared and look into many courses! Check out the time of classes if you want to maybe structure some days off during the week. Also, if you want to "balance" the work-load, you may be able to read from the description of examination how much work is in the course and when.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was never too advanced to be able to follow. I had a lot of professors with interesting experience from institutions or research which made the classes very interesting most of the time.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: All classes have 2-hour duration and don't include any breaks (if lucky, maybe 5 minutes halfway). For some of my classes, it was mainly teacher monologue, and student engagement was limited to weekly student presentations and sometimes debates, but never in-class group work for example.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
EU Security and Foreign Policies
EU Challenges (migration, climate change, populism)
Comparative Politics
Learning from The South (The Horn Of Africa)
Planetary health and epidemics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the course with focus on the Horn of Africa! The teacher was very interesting and invested in her field of research.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Prepare for a work-load heavier than the average exchange semester (even though it definitely depends on the courses you pick)
Expect that the housing process can be difficult unless you get a room in the Cité Universitaire or just find something else by luck :)
Get a bike if you feel comfortable to do so! Swapfiets costs 21€ a month. It is a great way of getting to know the city. Most areas are safe for biking, even though you have to learn how to 'navigate' in the Parisian rules.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No comment

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in Paris and learning about the city and country

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In my case, the work-load. I spent many (!) hours studying, especially the last month and a half.
